newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil ambassador to Peru among hostages, unhurt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil ambassador to Peru among hostages, unhurt.

text.p: Brazil said on Wednesday it would send an envoy to Peru to take part in possible talks with leftist rebels holding 200 hostages, including Brazil's ambassador, at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.
"Until now, it appears that the Peruvian government has shown no inclination to negotiate," said Sebastiao do Rego Barros, general secretary of the Foreign Ministry.
"From the Brazilian point of view, we are getting prepared to have negotiators ready should they be needed," Barros said.
Guerrillas of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) stormed the residence on Tuesday night and threatened to kill hostages if Peru did not agree to release jailed guerrillas.
Asked if Brazil had asked Peru to negotiate, Barros said: "We don't want to give any information that might seem to help the kidnappers."
He said the kidnapping of a Brazilian ambassador in Colombia in the 1970s was successfully resolved with the help of a special envoy from Brasilia.

Brazil's ambassador to Peru, Carlos Luiz Peres, spoke briefly by telephone with his wife, who was released earlier Wednesday, and was forced by rebels to pass on a message calling on Peru to negotiate, Barros said.
